clue.text: Ranting about area in short column

indicators.note: about here means going round, so the ranting word wraps the area letter

parts.note: ranting and blustering both mean talking loudly and aggressively

explanation.surface: A speaker raves about some region in a brief newspaper piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Column' looks like a newspaper column, but it is a stubby architectural one, the kind found in a row holding up a handrail.
explanation.definitionFit: A baluster is one of the short pillars supporting a rail on a staircase or balcony.

clue.text: A learner judged — without reaching conclusion, however

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate letter

indicators.note: never reaching its end means the final letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: to have thought something is to have judged it so

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a learner was assessed but the verdict never quite arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without reaching conclusion' cuts the last T from THOUGHT, leaving THOUGH.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words introduce a contrast with what came before, as conjunctions of concession.

clue.text: Without objection, trying to support amateur?

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath, so it comes second

parts.note: someone who is not a pro, playfully written as un-pro
trying something out is testing it

explanation.surface: An amateur is being backed up by a trial run, and nobody complains.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the invented word UN-PRO for an amateur, someone who is not professional.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something without protest means doing it without raising any objection.

clue.text: Rhythmic performance of tribal leader caught, included in record

indicators.note: being included in something means sitting inside it, so these letters go into the record

parts.note: a tape is a recording
Dan was the founding patriarch of one of the twelve tribes of Israel
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A chief's display is captured on a recording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'included in' puts the leader and caught letters inside the record. 'Tribal leader' is not a chief: Dan founded one of the twelve tribes of Israel in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Tap dancing is a stage routine beating out rhythms with metal-tipped shoes.

clue.text: Provided with different plans as new guard turned up

indicators.note: in a down clue turning upward reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: a prison guard is a warder

explanation.surface: Fresh arrangements are drawn up because a new sentry has arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses WARDER into REDRAW; 'as' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan that has been redrawn has been given a fresh design or layout.

clue.text: Hurriedly write second slow movement

parts.note: a crawl is a very slow pace

explanation.surface: A writer dashes off a note during a leisurely piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slow movement' suggests a musical adagio, but it is just a crawl.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrawl is to write quickly and carelessly, producing untidy handwriting.

clue.text: Cake, a little one

definitions.meaning: a yeast sponge soaked in syrup
a pet word for a baby or small child

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a syrup-soaked sponge dessert and, informally, an infant.

clue.text: Separated couples in crude ad he attacked — a no-win situation

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the phrase, split into separate two-letter pairs across the words

explanation.surface: Couples split up after a man assaulted a rude advert, and nobody came out ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits in cruDE AD HE ATtacked, split into the pairs DE, AD, HE, AT.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead heat is a race finishing level, so no single competitor wins.

clue.text: Move up case that's rearranged, with others put back

indicators.note: being rearranged means these letters are put into a new order
putting it back means the abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: et al is Latin for and others

explanation.surface: A legal case is reshuffled upward, with other cases pushed later.
explanation.walkthrough: CASE rearranged gives ESCA; ET AL put back gives LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To escalate is to increase or rise in level, intensity or rank.

clue.text: Knock out high card in bridge

definitions.meaning: in boxing a fighter who ... his opponent wins by knockout
in bridge a ... is a card that prevents the opponents running a suit

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both halting a boxer for good and a bridge card that blocks a suit.

clue.text: Author's condition, looking exhausted

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition reads as the author is

parts.note: a rider is a condition added to an agreement
haggard means looking worn out

explanation.surface: A writer's health is poor and the strain shows on their face.
explanation.walkthrough: H. Rider Haggard wrote King Solomon's Mines; 'condition' is a proviso, not an illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Rider Haggard was a Victorian novelist of adventure stories.

clue.text: Measure of goodness? It was used to evaluate currencies

definitions.meaning: a benchmark of excellence against which others are judged

definitions.text: It was used to evaluate currencies
definitions.meaning: the monetary system that fixed a currency's value to a weight of bullion

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both a supreme benchmark and the old monetary system pegging money to bullion.

clue.text: Chicken, one ruling the roost?

definitions.meaning: an ornamental breed of domestic fowl
a Muslim sovereign, playfully seen as the boss of a henhouse

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a Turkish breed of fowl and an Islamic monarch.

clue.text: Noted wit has pound provided inside for animals

indicators.note: inside means these letters are placed within the wit's name

parts.note: Oscar Wilde was famous for his epigrams
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling
provided that means if

explanation.surface: A celebrated humorist has a pound if needed for the creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' places the pound and provided letters within the wit's name; 'has' is only a link. The noted wit is Oscar, famous for his epigrams.
explanation.definitionFit: Wildlife means undomesticated creatures living in their natural habitat, collectively.

clue.text: With maximum possible speed, rush to subdue

parts.note: c is the physicists' symbol for the speed of light, the cosmic limit
to hasten is to rush

explanation.surface: Hurrying at top speed in order to bring someone under control.
explanation.walkthrough: C, the speed of light, is the fastest anything can go.
explanation.definitionFit: To chasten is to restrain or humble someone, bringing them into check.

clue.text: One outer garment pulled up over single undergarment

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits over, above, the second
in a down clue pulling up reads the pieces from bottom to top

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a mac is a raincoat
sole means single or only

explanation.surface: A coat is hauled up over a lone piece of underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulled up' turns I and MAC together into CAMI; SOLE goes below.
explanation.definitionFit: A camisole is a loose sleeveless top worn as lingerie under clothes.

clue.text: Cut, offering sitter —- catch initially fumbled

indicators.note: a fumbled thing is mishandled, so these letters are jumbled
initially points to the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A fielder drops an easy chance, a sitter, at the crease.
explanation.walkthrough: SITTER and C (first of catch) are rearranged. A sitter is cricket slang for a very easy catch.
explanation.definitionFit: To trisect is to cut something into three equal parts.

clue.text: Core of belief in area of faith

indicators.note: in means the core letters are placed within the area word

parts.note: a region is an area

indicators.note: the core of a word is its central letters

explanation.surface: Central to belief in a domain of faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the central two letters of belief inside the area word. 'Core of' takes the middle pair because belief has six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A religion is a system of faith and worship.

clue.text: Radio or TV programme using singers to what extent?

parts.note: chats are small songbirds such as the stonechat
how asks to what degree

explanation.surface: A broadcast featuring vocalists asks how far it can go.
explanation.definitionFit: A chat show is a broadcast in which a host interviews guests.

clue.text: Japan, perhaps, receiving name in European language

indicators.note: receiving means taking the letter in, so it goes inside

parts.note: japan is a black lacquer, an example of a finish

explanation.surface: The country of Japan takes in a name in some tongue of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Japan' is a glossy varnish, not the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Finnish is the national tongue spoken in Finland.

clue.text: Musical heroine with cape greeting Mexican players

parts.note: Maria is the heroine of The Sound of Music and West Side Story
C is the map abbreviation for cape
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: A stage-show leading lady in a cloak welcomes a band from Mexico.
explanation.definitionFit: A mariachi is a Mexican street band of strolling musicians.

clue.text: Large vehicle showed up around parking meter, finally

indicators.note: around means the arrival word goes round the parking letter

parts.note: came means arrived or showed up
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A big van appeared near a parking meter at last.
explanation.walkthrough: CAME goes around P; R ends meter.
explanation.definitionFit: A camper is a motor vehicle fitted out for living in on holiday.

clue.text: Pack animals not long returning, carrying article

indicators.note: carrying means holding the article inside
returning means the word is read backwards

parts.note: something not long is small
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Beasts of burden on a short trip home bear a load.
explanation.walkthrough: SMALL returning gives LLAMS, holding A.
explanation.definitionFit: Llamas are South American camelids used to carry loads.

clue.text: Carefully controlled bloke getting on coach at the front

indicators.note: being at the front means this piece comes first

parts.note: a stage or stagecoach is a horse-drawn coach
a bloke is a man
getting on means growing old, aged

explanation.surface: An elderly man boards the bus at the front, under tight control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting on' is not boarding but growing old.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stage-managed is orchestrated behind the scenes to look spontaneous.

clue.text: Primate securing singular place in church

indicators.note: securing means holding it fast inside

parts.note: an ape is a primate
S is the grammar abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A monkey grabs a unique spot in a chapel.
explanation.definitionFit: The apse is the semicircular recess at the east end of a church.

clue.text: One seen outside hospital for pain

indicators.note: outside means the one word wraps around the hospital letter

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards
H is the road-sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Someone seen outside a hospital because they are hurting.
explanation.definitionFit: An ache is a continuous dull pain.

clue.text: Lacking energy, start to get back on even keel

annotationWithheld.why: Lacking energy, start to get back on even keel: 'on even keel' gives the second sense, but no parse accounts for 'start to get back' as held; possibly OCR garble
annotationWithheld.clue: Lacking energy, start to get back on even keel

clue.text: Leave one's cards on the table

definitions.meaning: to leave something to heirs, bequeath
a card hand laid face down on the table

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to bequeath to a successor, and also a hand of cards laid down.
